analyst_view.overall: Early view: Galatasaray lead by three points and are 41 league games unbeaten at home, but they will be without Victor Osimhen (knee surgery on 7 November) and Rafael Leao (severe muscle strain against Amed), and they play Aston Villa in the Champions League three days later. Samsunspor are 17th; Nenad Bjelica's side ended an eight-game losing run by beating Konyaspor 1-0 just before the break. Captain Abdulkerim Bardakci completed his ban against Amed and should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. I lean a bit lower: Galatasaray still scored four against Amed without Osimhen, but losing Leao too and the Aston Villa game three days later make rotation likely, and Samsunspor kept a clean sheet in Bjelica's first win.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, mostly Galatasaray's. They won only three against an Amed side that attacked them, but Samsunspor are likely to sit deep and defend their box, which usually pushes Galatasaray's count up, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and I lean lower. Galatasaray were not booked at all against Amed, and Davinson Sanchez and Roland Sallai are one yellow away from a ban that would rule them out of the Besiktas derby, so they have reason to stay careful; most cards should come from Samsunspor's defending.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, 22.8 of them Galatasaray's. I lean lower because the two forwards who shoot most are out and Okan Buruk may rest players before Aston Villa; Galatasaray had 17 shots against Amed, and 20-plus without Osimhen is a stretch even against a weaker side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Galatasaray hit the target six times against Amed, and with Osimhen and Leao out I expect seven or eight from them plus a couple from Samsunspor, slightly under the number.
